text.p: Italy's debt market ended a lacklustre session with Btp futures little changed on previous closing levels. Traders said the market had put the downturn of Monday and Tuesday behind it but had no clear direction and was just holding in line with other European bond markets.

Market attention was still focused on the dollar's strength which was preventing European bonds from moving higher. "Those hoping for statements from the German government which might give the mark a boost have been disappointed," one trader said.

The German government today reminded the markets that the Group of Seven said in February -- when dollar/mark traded down in the mid 1.60s -- that the mark's appreciation had been fully corrected and that dollar and sterling reflected the trend of the economies of the respective countries.
"This has only confirmed market doubts over the future strength of the mark and the euro," one specialist said.

Traders said there was uncertainty about Btp direction, noting the September contract had neither broken support at 135.40 nor resistance in the 135.70 area during the session. But the contract began rising above this level in Liffe APT trade.
